title: Decouple prefill worker queue with priority-stealing and opportunistic decode forwarding
author: Laura Chen
description:
Context: We observed end-to-end tail latency regressions when prefill-heavy workloads saturate GPU workers: long-running prefill kernels block decode slots and cause increased P99s for short chat/turn requests. Prior PRs improved prefill chunking and overlap, but customer workloads with mixed short/long requests still see variability.

What this PR does: 1) Decouples prefill task enqueueing from GPU worker execution by introducing a deferred prefill queue (DPQ) and a small pool of prefill workers dedicated to short prefill fragments. The DPQ supports priority-stealing: short, latency-sensitive prefills are stamped with HIGH priority and can steal capacity from background low-priority prefill tasks. 2) Adds opportunistic decode forwarding: when decode workers detect idle cycles (e.g., micro-slices between large kernel launches), they can pull already-prefilled KV windows and immediately service small decode-only requests without waiting for the full prefill pipeline handoff. This reduces scheduling hops and avoids long-tail handoffs. 3) Implements soft KV-cache pinning for recently-used prefixes: small, frequently-accessed KV shards are kept hot in LRU-protected memory for a short TTL so opportunistic decode forwarding finds warm state. 4) Exposes three server flags to control behavior: --dpq-max-concurrency, --dpq-steal-threshold, --kvpin-ttl-ms. Defaults tuned conservatively to avoid regressions.

Behavioral notes and safety: - PREFILL semantics are unchanged (deterministic outputs). This is purely scheduling/placement and cache hinting. - Feature gated: dpq and kvpin are enabled behind runtime flags and disabled by default for Dedicated customers until validated. - Includes new tracing spans (dpq.enqueue, dpq.steal, decode.forward) and metrics (dpq_queue_time_ms, dpq_steals_total, kvpin_hits).

Benchmark results (microbench, representative mix):
- Baseline: 99th latency = 512ms, throughput = 540 tok/s (mixed short+long)
- With DPQ + opportunistic forwarding: 99th latency = 312ms (-39%), throughput = 570 tok/s (+5.5%)
- KV-pin hit rate under steady state: 78% for top-10 prefixes (config: kvpin-ttl-ms=1500)

Testing and CI: unit tests for DPQ queue semantics and priority-stealing; integration test harness extends perf-canary scenarios to include mixed short/long request mixes. Small e2e run against a 4-GPU node showed no correctness regressions. CI initially failed lint (prefetch variable name), fixed in follow-up commit.

Checklist:
- [x] Add DPQ implementation and worker scheduling changes
- [x] Add opportunistic decode forwarding and tracing spans
- [x] KV pin cache with expiration and metrics
- [x] Unit + integration tests
- [x] Perf microbench and summary included here
- [x] Documentation: runtime flags and recommended defaults added to runtime/README.md

Related: builds on previous work around prefill chunking and overlap (see ENG-1510, ENG-1609), but intentionally focuses on scheduling/pinning rather than kernel changes.

Notes for reviewers: pay special attention to the DPQ stealing logic (prefill/queue_manager.cc) and the correctness of KV pin eviction under memory pressure (kvcache/kv_pin_manager.cc).

review_comments:
Diego Martinez: 'Can you add a safety valve so dpq-steal doesn't starve background long-running prefill batches under extreme short-request bursts?'

Laura Chen (author): 'Added dpq-steal-threshold and a dynamic backoff that reduces steal rate after sustained steals (>1s sustain). See queue_manager.cc:StealBackoffPolicy.'

Sofia Patel: 'Bench numbers look promising. Please add a test that simulates memory pressure to validate kvpin eviction correctness.'

Laura Chen: 'Added integration test that toggles artificial memory pressure and asserts kvpin does not exceed configured memory budget; eviction semantics validated.'

Arjun Rao: 'Minor: prefer exponential-moving-average for dpq_queue_time_ms aggregation to reduce noisy spikes.'

Laura Chen: 'Swapped sum/count to EMA in metrics registry, updated tests and dashboards.'
release_notes: Improves tail latency for mixed short/long prefill workloads by introducing a deferred prefill queue with priority-stealing and opportunistic decode forwarding. Adds KV-cache pinning for hot prefixes and runtime flags to tune behavior. Backward-compatible and feature-gated behind runtime flags.
notes_for_ops: Feature is off by default for Dedicated; enable via --enable-dpq and configure --dpq-max-concurrency (default 4) and --kvpin-ttl-ms (default 1500). Monitor dpq_queue_time_ms and kvpin_hits. If dpq_steals_total grows rapidly and dpq_queue_time_ms increases, decrease dpq-steal-threshold or disable dpq.
changelog_entry: perf: schedule-level optimization - deferred prefill queue, opportunistic decode forwarding, kvcache pinning (ergonomics flags)
